operational-example.copy: Use Avatar to identify a person, driver, approver, or system actor when name recognition helps the task.

scenario.title: Driver identity cluster
rationale: Avatar makes accountable people scannable in tables, approvals, chat, audit, and driver flows.
The ZIP reference uses deterministic initials, circular sizing, optional image, and presence dot.
Use text labels near Avatar when identity must be unambiguous.

items.rule: Circular identity container with fixed density.
Photo is preferred; initials are deterministic fallback.
Optional online, busy, or offline status.
Name is exposed when Avatar conveys identity.

accessibility.statePrecedence: disabled, busy, online, offline, default, unknown
items: Expose the person name when Avatar carries identity.
Do not rely on initials as the only label in critical flows.
Presence color needs text or nearby status when status matters.
Image alt equals the represented person name.

variants.copy: Avatar variants describe source and grouping: initials, image, status, group, and system.

states.copy: Avatar states communicate presence, busy work, offline state, disabled identity, and default availability.

variant-state-behavior.copy: Variant defines identity source; state defines availability and whether presence is meaningful.

full-width.copy: Avatar never stretches full width; the containing row or card owns layout.

responsive-layout-patterns.copy: Density changes with density, but accessible identity must stay available in nearby text.

viewport-organization.copy: Use Avatar as an identity anchor inside rows, cards, chat, and approval flows.

items.title: Phone
items.rule: Use comfortable density with visible name.

items.title: Tablet
items.rule: Use status only when the task needs availability.

items.title: Desktop
items.rule: Use compact-density avatars in dense tables with text labels.

playground.copy: Use the playground to verify identity source, density mapping, status, and disabled state.

api-foundations.copy: Avatar API exposes name, src, density, status, and state while Design System foundations own identity, presence, shape, tone, and accessibility.

props.name: density
props.notes: Density-aware scale: sm, md, lg, or xl.

props.name: state
props.notes: Disabled or unknown state when presence is not the state source.

groups.title: Use
items: Use for people, teams, and system actors.
Keep names visible near critical avatars.

groups.title: Avoid
items: Do not use color alone for presence.
Do not use Avatar as decoration in dense docs.

groups.title: Review
items: Check alt text, fallback initials, status meaning, and small-density legibility.

miel.copy: MIEL treats Avatar as identity evidence: agents may place it when an actor matters, but humans confirm privacy, status meaning, and whether a name must be visible.
canDecide: Use Avatar for drivers, approvers, support agents, and system actors.
Use initials fallback when no image exists.
Use small density in dense tables with a text label.
mustAsk: Presence status changes permissions, availability, or escalation.
The identity is sensitive or masked.
A group or overflow rule is required.
rejectIf: The avatar replaces the visible name in a critical decision.
miel.handoff: I am using Avatar to identify an actor. Please confirm visible name, privacy level, image use, and whether presence status is meaningful.
